title: Responder Snaplet: micro-brief and guided alert authoring
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Introduce a compact Responder Snaplet: an inline micro-brief that appears during alert creation and in on-call handoff flows. The snaplet surfaces the on-call owner, a 2-line runbook excerpt, one-click postmortem deep-link, and a lightweight cost/latency preview for the alert route. It also powers a first-time guided tour for alert authoring that walks new users through structured conditions, SLO guardrails, and postmortem attachments.
background: Current alert composer is full-page and assumes a seasoned user. We lack a focused mini-surface for rapid handoffs or for responders to capture incident context when creating follow-up alerts. PMs have reported slow handoffs and missing postmortem links in 18% of incidents in Q3 retrospective; design research indicates a short inline surface would reduce friction and make linking artifacts explicit.
goals: Reduce time-to-link postmortem or runbook during alert creation
Provide a compact on-call snapshot in the composer and handoff drawer
Lower cognitive load for first-time alert authors through a guided tour
Show immediate cost/latency signal tied to alert routing choices
acceptance_criteria: Snaplet appears as an optional compact strip in alert composer and handoff drawer
Contains: owner badge, 2-line runbook excerpt (editable), postmortem deep-link button, cost/latency preview badge
Guided tour walkthrough completes in <= 90s with mock data and leaves no modal traps
Keyboard accessible and meets WCAG AA for contrast and focus order
All actions generate analytics events (snaplet_shown, snaplet_edit, postmortem_link_added)
decisions: Favor a non-modal inline snaplet to avoid interrupting the authoring flow
Show only a 2-line runbook excerpt with a ‘View full runbook’ deep link to reduce clutter
Cost preview will be a relative delta badge (low/medium/high) not an estimated $ to avoid noisy estimates in early rollouts
Guided tour will be opt-in for first 3 uses and available from composer help menu thereafter
tradeoffs: Inline surface reduces context switches but consumes vertical real estate on small screens
Relative cost badges reduce accuracy expectations but avoid heavy infra calculations; engineering will expose detailed cost tooling behind the badge
Making runbook excerpts editable increases copy complexity and permission checks; initial MVP will show an edit link that opens the runbook editor (owned by docs team)
security_notes: Postmortem deep links must respect RBAC; links to private Confluence docs should be proxied or tokenized. Coordinate with Security for telemetry and link sanitization.
